body:
## Problem

Known limit of the #593 fix (PR #619, "Known limits"): the fold's merged-head check is by commit ancestry (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`, `template/src/pdca_harness/integrate.py:451-459` on branch `fix/593-stack-mode-append-only-fold-real-base-prs`). If someone reverts a merged prerequisite on the base, the base still "has" the head, so the fold merges the base in and **the revert with it**.

Reproduced on real git by the final adversary review: fold [A] → T1; push a fixup to fix/A; merge fix/A into `main`; delete fix/A; `git revert -m 1` that merge on `main`; fold [A, B] with `{TARGET: T1}`. The fold passes, merges `main` in, and the line ends with `['b.txt', 'base.txt']`: A's change is gone, not only the fixup. B, which depends on A, builds without A, and stderr says "the merged work reaches pdca-integration/main through origin/main", which is false. The same happens when a base merge brings in a revert of any *other* bundle already on the line.

Same failure class as #593 round 6 (a prerequisite silently dropped).

## Done when

Decide: stop the fold when taking in the base removes a bundle's own paths from the line (e.g. compare the line before and after the base merge on each folded bundle's paths), or accept and document it. Either way, the stderr line must not claim the work reaches the base when it doesn't. A real-git test pins the revert case.

Found by the eduralph/pdca-pdca Act review of 2026-10-02 (issue_593 final adversary review + PR #619 Known limits).
title: stack mode: a reverted prerequisite on the base passes the fold's ancestry check, so the fold takes the revert in and dependents build without it
